releases.name: 2.0.0: priced accounting and Console calibration
releases.notes:
## Minimal install

This release ships a package with exactly what the skill needs at runtime, plus the license:

- `opencode-go-model-picker-2.0.0-min.zip` → `SKILL.md`, `references/`, `scripts/`, `LICENSE`

Unzip it into `~/.config/opencode/skills/` (Linux/macOS) or `%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode\skills\` (Windows) so the folder is named `opencode-go-model-picker`. No dependencies, no build step.

Chinese documentation: [README-ZH.md](https://github.com/sogeisetsu/opencode-go-model-picker/blob/main/README-ZH.md).

---
## [2.0.0] - 2026-10-30

### Added

- `references/quota-math.md` and `scripts/quota-math.mjs`: the one priced-accounting
 implementation. Formula v2 prices each assistant message on its own timestamp,
 picks the price by the request's prompt length when a model has context-length
 tiers, applies the peak-hour multiplier only to models that declare one, and
 bills cache writes on the models that charge for them. Reasoning tokens are
 billed at the output rate, checked message-by-message against the provider's own
 per-message cost — omitting them under-prices a message by 4–34%. Derived quantities
 (share of cap, the three independent pool windows, sessions per window, official
 and observed capacity), the pool reverse-solve order, the eight known gaps, and
 the degradation rules for every missing field.
- `references/console-mcp.md` and `scripts/probe-console.mjs`: the five Console MCP
 states (`authorized` / `gated` / `unauthenticated` / `absent` / `unknown`),
 decided cheapest-first (in-run tool result → `opencode mcp list` → config → one
 `initialize` request), with the fixed per-state guidance copy, the three-level
 fallback, and the enabling steps for the OpenCode CLI and OpenChamber. The probe
 never prints a token and never classifies a network failure as "not set up".
- `scripts/calibrate-usage.mjs`: sums the local OpenCode SQLite database per agent
 and model, compares it with the Console's own cost to measure the bias (warning
 when it drifts more than 10%), reverse-solves the plan pool in the documented
 order, projects month-end occupancy from the billing cycle, and — with `--write`
 — stores `plan`, `models.<id>.billing`, `usage.agentSplit` and `calibration` in
 the snapshot.
- `references/model-prices.json` gained `cacheWritePer1M`, `ctxTiers`, `capUsd`,
 `peak`, `promoUntil` and a verified `status` per model, plus current
 `planVerifiedAt` dates. It is now the single home of price, cap, context tiers
 and peak hours.
- Snapshot schema v3: `plan.go`, `models.<id>.billing`, `availability`,
 `capabilities` (per-capability source + `verifiedAt`), `usage.agentSplit` and
 `calibration`.
- `scripts/discover-agents.mjs` now reports a run-level `deadChainIds` summary
 (`missing-from-catalog`, `retired`, `registry-missing`, `registry-deprecated`),
 warns on a shared chain head (`contention`) because the per-model cap is shared,
 and warns per agent when a Go id's catalog status is retired (`catalog`).
- `references/data-sources.md` gained a Console-bill (priority 0) section, a
 two-quota-layer section, official-vs-observed request counts, and a dated
 capability/compliance table (image input, training, retention, availability).
- `quota-math.mjs` reports seed freshness — `verifiedAt` (the newest
 `planVerifiedAt` / `priceVerifiedAt` in the table), `ageDays` and `stale` — and
 marks a seed older than seven days as expired, so an offline run labels its
 numbers instead of presenting them as current. `calibrate-usage.mjs` reports the
 same under `prices`.

### Changed

- The report now opens with a mandatory `Basis:` line (`Console bill
 (authoritative)` / `Estimate` / `Uncalibrated`) and one denominator for the whole
 table, and the table columns are the priced ones: headroom, accounted
 `$/session` (median · P90), share of the model cap, 10 runs as a share of the
 three pool windows, actual monthly occupancy, and why.
- A new `Usage evidence` block is mandatory: last-30-days spend and requests, a
 last-7-days pace with a month-end projection, the count of candidates without an
 ELO, the dead chain ids for this run, and the main agents' share of spend.
- `SKILL.md`'s workflow was reordered to discover → probe Console → read the bill
 and calibrate → refresh the snapshot → detect plan changes → allocate → build
 chains → output → stop, and now ends with nine explicit self-checks.
- `scripts/refresh-prices.mjs` reads the cache-write price and the context-length
 tiers from models.dev, and carries the plan-side constants (`capUsd` /
 `monthlyLimitUsd`, `peak`, `promoUntil`, `estReq*`, `status`) through a rewrite,
 so regenerating the seed no longer deletes them.
- `calibrate-usage.mjs --write` raises `schemaVersion` to 3 when it writes v3 keys;
 an existing v2 file is read as-is (every v3 key is optional).
- `references/agent-sources.md` states that a native `agent.<name>.model` cannot
 express a chain, and points at the chain-capable source when failover is wanted.
- Stale plan facts from the 2026-09/10 verifications were corrected against the
 2026-10-30 plan page (the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 4x promo is gone; its cap is $80;
 peak/off-peak pricing replaced it).

### Breaking

- Output format: the previous table columns (role overview, capability focus,
 current model) are replaced by the priced columns, and the `Basis:` line is
 mandatory. A v1 report shape is no longer valid.
- Snapshot schema v2 → v3. Existing files stay readable, but the new fields are
 absent (hence `null`) until `calibrate-usage.mjs --write` runs.
- `references/model-prices.json` entry shape grew from 16 to 21 keys; anything
 reading that seed directly must tolerate the new fields.
- `SKILL.md`'s workflow numbering changed, so any prompt that referred to
 "step 2 = refresh" now points at the Console probe instead.

releases.name: v1.1.0
releases.notes:
# v1.1.0

`skill_management` gives every installed OpenCode skill a switch: list what is installed, find out
why one will not load, hide it from the model, and put it back. Disabling writes **one** global
`skill` permission rule — no skill file is ever moved, edited or deleted.

## Breaking change in 1.1.0

All four actions now return **one JSON object** instead of Markdown. The tool also declares an
`output` JSON Schema, so the host validates every result; this is a real structured tool result,
not Markdown wrapped in a JSON string.

- Envelope: `schemaVersion` (currently `1`), `action`, `ok`, `warnings`.
- Failures use `ok: false` plus `error: { code, message }`; success is no longer inferred from
 ✅ / ❌ in the text.
- `list` returns `callerAgent`, `summary`, `skills[]`, `config`, `sidecar`, `consistency`.
 `description` is still the first line, no longer truncated to 60 characters.
- `inspect` returns `skill`, `idDerivation`, `agents[]`, `caller`, `conclusion`. Missing and
 ambiguous targets use `skill_not_found` / `name_ambiguous`.
- `disable` / `enable` return `changed`, `reason`, `before`, `diff`, `verification`, `backup`,
 `sidecar`; `enable` also returns `location`, `rule`, `candidates`, `relatedRules`.
- `enable` now returns `ok: false` with `config_unparsable` when the target config cannot be
 parsed and no candidate rule exists, instead of claiming "nothing to change".

Nothing else broke: actions, input fields, the written rule shape, the same-line marker format
and the single-file layout are unchanged.

## Also since v1.0.0

- New bilingual documentation site (Astro + Starlight; English at the root, Chinese under
 `/zh-cn`): <https://sogeisetsu.github.io/opencode-skill-management/>
- README now documents the minimal npm install (`opencode plugin add`) and the package contents.
- Theme/language menus, card alignment and mobile spacing fixes on the docs site.

## What it does

| Action | What you get | Writes config |
|---|---|---|
| `list` | Every registered skill and its effective state for the **calling agent** (`available` / `disabled` / `ask`) | No |
| `inspect` | Why one skill is (not) usable: the matched rule, per-agent differences, how the id was derived | No |
| `disable` | Hidden from the model-visible list and rejected at load (`effect: "ask"` keeps it listed with confirmation) | Yes |
| `enable` | Deletes the one blocking rule, whoever wrote it | Yes |

Permissions are evaluated for the **calling agent only**: last match wins (`findLast`, with `*`
and `?` globs), and **no match falls back to `ask`, not `allow`**.

The rule `disable` writes is exactly this line (the trailing comment is the provenance marker
`enable` uses):

```jsonc
{ "action": "skill", "resource": "windows-shell", "effect": "deny" } // skill_management
```

Writes are atomic, preserve indentation, key order, line endings (CRLF/LF) and BOM, keep one
backup, and are verified by reloading the host and polling the caller's rule set; a write the
host did not pick up is rolled back.

## Usage

```text
skill_management({ action: "list" })
skill_management({ action: "inspect", id: "windows-shell" })
skill_management({ action: "disable", id: "windows-shell" })
skill_management({ action: "disable", id: "windows-shell", dryRun: true })
skill_management({ action: "disable", id: "windows-shell", effect: "ask" })
skill_management({ action: "enable", id: "windows-shell" })
```

A `list` result looks like this (abridged):

```json
{
 "schemaVersion": 1,
 "action": "list",
 "ok": true,
 "warnings": [],
 "callerAgent": { "id": "build", "verified": true },
 "summary": { "total": 29, "disabled": 1, "ask": 0, "diverged": 2, "derivedIds": 0 },
 "skills": [
 { "id": "windows-shell", "state": "available", "source": "config", "path": "..." },
 { "id": "pdf-tools", "state": "disabled", "source": "catalog", "path": "..." }
 ],
 "config": { "file": ".../opencode.jsonc", "hadPermissions": true, "notes": [] },
 "sidecar": { "file": ".../skill_management.state.json", "ok": true, "error": null },
 "consistency": { "staleSidecarIds": [], "unrecordedRules": [], "missingFromRegistry": [] }
}
```

Full field tables and error codes are on the four action pages of the docs site.

## Install

| Channel | Command / asset | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **npm (recommended)** | `opencode plugin add opencode-skill-management@1.1.0` | Installs the package and registers it in the global config; no token needed |
| git spec | `opencode plugin add github:sogeisetsu/opencode-skill-management` | Bypasses the npm registry |
| Single file | asset `skill_management.js` | Drop it into `<config>/plugins/`; best for offline use |
| npm tarball | asset `opencode-skill-management-1.1.0.tgz` | The same tarball npm publishes; for auditing or internal mirrors |

Verify it loaded in a **new process**:

```pwsh
opencode plugin list --builtin
# skill_management 1.1.0 opencode-skill-management@1.1.0
```

## Compatibility and verification

- Targets OpenCode V2; 1.1.0 was accepted on host **2.0.32** on Windows and Linux.
- `node tools/verify.mjs`: **260 assertions** pass, entirely against a temporary config directory.
- New-process runs against the real host returned parseable JSON for both `list` and the
 "skill not found" error path, and both passed the host's `output` validation.
- One file, pure Node built-ins, no runtime dependencies, no shell calls.

**Full diff**: <https://github.com/sogeisetsu/opencode-skill-management/compare/v1.0.0...v1.1.0>

en.headline: 18 own commits plus 26 automated; two releases and two issue actions
en.summary: **18 own commits** were made across four repositories, plus 26 automated commits by `github-actions[bot]`. In `sogeisetsu/opencode-go-model-picker`, 8 commits added priced accounting, Console calibration, output v2, expired-seed labeling, and documentation on request derivation and cost sources. In `sogeisetsu/opencode-skill-management`, 7 commits made the four actions return one JSON object with a declared output schema and updated the bilingual docs, README, changelog, and acceptance records to `v1.1.0`. In `sogeisetsu/sogeisetsu`, 2 commits tightened `AGENTS.md`, moved model-selection testing into `MODELS.md`, and added Xiaohongshu Dots as a daily-report fallback; in `sogeisetsu/opencode-agent-sandbox`, 1 commit corrected schema and registration details in the V2 plugin and tool-registration findings. The user opened or closed 2 issues: they opened `openchamber/openchamber` issue #5935, “Settings > MCP omits the Console MCP server that OpenCode adds at runtime,” and commented on issue #5879 about viewing and clearing task temp files. Issue #5935 received replies from `openchamber-bot[bot]`, which traced the cause to config-only page data, and `yulia-ivashko`, who requested triage. Separately, `btriapitsyn` closed `openchamber/openchamber` issue #5680 about the outdated session-retention hint.

releaseNotes.summary: This release adds `references/quota-math.md` and `scripts/quota-math.mjs` for per-message priced accounting, including context-length tiers, peak-hour multipliers, cache-write billing, reasoning-token checks, and seed freshness with expiry after seven days. It adds `references/console-mcp.md` and `scripts/probe-console.mjs` to distinguish five Console MCP states without printing tokens, plus `scripts/calibrate-usage.mjs` to compare local SQLite usage with Console cost, reverse-solve plan pools, and optionally write calibration data. The report now requires a `Basis:` line and a `Usage evidence` block, and the snapshot schema advances to v3 with billing, availability, capabilities, agent-split usage, and calibration fields.

All four actions now return one JSON object instead of Markdown and declare an `output` JSON Schema for host validation. The envelope includes `schemaVersion`, `action`, `ok`, and `warnings`; failures use `ok: false` with an `error` object, and `enable` reports `config_unparsable` when no candidate rule can be found. The release also adds a bilingual Astro and Starlight documentation site, documents minimal npm installation and package contents, and fixes theme menus, card alignment, and mobile spacing.

zh.headline: 18 次本人提交，另有 26 次自动提交；两次发布与两项 issue 操作
zh.summary: 当天在四个仓库完成 **18 次本人提交**，另有 26 次由 `github-actions[bot]` 自动提交。`sogeisetsu/opencode-go-model-picker` 的 8 次提交加入计价核算、Console 校准、输出 v2、过期价格种子标记，并补充请求推导与费用来源文档。`sogeisetsu/opencode-skill-management` 的 7 次提交让四个动作输出单个 JSON 对象并声明输出 schema，同时将中英文文档、README、CHANGELOG 和验收记录更新至 `v1.1.0`。`sogeisetsu/sogeisetsu` 的 2 次提交收紧 `AGENTS.md`、将选型实测移入 `MODELS.md`，并接入小红书 Dots 作为日报链尾兜底；`sogeisetsu/opencode-agent-sandbox` 的 1 次提交纠正了 V2 插件与工具注册实测中的 schema 和 Registration 误传。用户新开或关闭 2 个 issue：新开 `openchamber/openchamber` 的 #5935“Settings > MCP omits the Console MCP server that OpenCode adds at runtime”，并在 #5879 评论任务临时文件的查看与清理。#5935 收到 `openchamber-bot[bot]` 回复，其将原因追溯到页面仅使用配置层数据；`yulia-ivashko` 则请求进行分类处理。此外，`btriapitsyn` 关闭了 `openchamber/openchamber` 的 #5680，该 issue 涉及过时的会话保留提示。

releaseNotes.summary: 本次发布新增 `references/quota-math.md` 与 `scripts/quota-math.mjs`，按消息时间戳计价，支持上下文长度分层、高峰时段倍率、缓存写入计费、推理 token 校验，并在七天后标记价格种子过期。新增 `references/console-mcp.md` 与 `scripts/probe-console.mjs`，用于区分五种 Console MCP 状态且不打印 token；`scripts/calibrate-usage.mjs` 则对比本地 SQLite 用量与 Console 费用、反解计划池，并可写入校准数据。报告现在必须包含 `Basis:` 行和 `Usage evidence` 块，快照 schema 升级至 v3，加入计费、可用性、能力、按 agent 拆分用量和校准字段。

四个动作现在统一返回单个 JSON 对象而非 Markdown，并声明 `output` JSON Schema 供宿主校验。结果信封包含 `schemaVersion`、`action`、`ok` 和 `warnings`，失败使用 `ok: false` 与 `error` 对象；`enable` 在找不到候选规则时返回 `config_unparsable`。本次发布还新增基于 Astro 与 Starlight 的中英文文档站，补充最小 npm 安装与包文件说明，并修复主题菜单、卡片对齐和移动端间距。
